steps.name: Pre-session — Welcome slide (put this up before people arrive)
steps.say: Nothing to say yet — this is what people see as they trickle in and join. Run this step, then just wait; move on to the icebreaker once most of the room is in.

steps.name: 0:00 — Icebreaker: one word
steps.say: Add one word to the shared board: what's your current relationship with AI in your teaching, right now, honestly?

steps.name: 0:05 — Baseline gut-check
steps.say: Set your status: doing ok = I feel clear about what's allowed right now, confused = somewhat unsure, stuck = pretty lost, away = haven't thought about it yet. No wrong answer — we compare this again at the end.

steps.name: 0:08 — Guide page: Understanding Generative AI
steps.say: Quick framing before we dive in: generative AI predicts likely words from patterns, not facts — that's also why it can be confidently wrong.

steps.name: 0:10 — Order the five AI usage levels
steps.say: Drag these five statements into order, from most restrictive (no AI at all) to most open (AI as a creative partner).

steps.name: 0:18 — Reveal the scale order
steps.say: Let's check the answer together.

steps.name: 0:19 — Guide page: Evaluating AI Use
steps.say: Here's the Guide page behind what we just did, if you want the fuller version later.

steps.name: 0:20 — Match the concern to the discipline
steps.say: Different fields worry about different things when it comes to AI. Drag each concern into the discipline most likely to raise it — a couple of pieces are decoys.

steps.name: 0:28 — Reveal the discipline matches
steps.say: Let's check which ones landed correctly.

steps.name: 0:29 — Guide page: Ethics and Impact of AI
steps.say: This is the page those discipline concerns are drawn from.

steps.name: 0:30 — Facts worth remembering
steps.say: Quick reinforcement round — drag the right piece into each blank. There are a couple of decoys here too.

steps.name: 0:38 — Reveal the facts
steps.say: Let's see the score and read the completed paragraph together.

steps.name: 0:39 — Guide page: Using AI in the Classroom
steps.say: The page behind the redesign task you're about to do.

steps.name: 0:40 — Redesign in groups: make groups and show the task
steps.say: Find your group on this tab — the task is right there too, and it'll stay visible the whole time, even once the timer's running.

actions.prompt:
Spend 10 minutes reflecting on how a course concept connects to a real-world example, and be ready to talk about what you noticed.

In your group, rewrite these instructions twice:

Level 1 — AI only for planning.
The final reflection must be entirely the student's own thinking.

Level 3 — AI used extensively.
The student must direct and justify how they used it.

Post your Level 3 version as a sticky note on the Whiteboard tab.

steps.name: 0:41 — Start the timer
steps.say: 7 minutes, starting now. Switch to the Whiteboard tab whenever you're ready to post your note — this screen and the timer will still be here when you switch back.

steps.name: 0:48 — Reset the timer after debrief
steps.say: Let's hear two or three Level 3 notes out loud before we move on.

steps.name: 0:49 — Guide pages: Tools and Policies, Building Skills
steps.say: Two more pages worth knowing exist, briefly — which tools are approved, and where to go to get better at this.

steps.name: 0:49 (b) — Guide page: Building AI Skills
steps.say: And this one, for whenever you want to go deeper yourself.

steps.name: 0:50 — Closing self-check
steps.say: Rate yourself on these right now — no one else sees your name attached to your answer, just the shape of the room.

steps.name: 0:57 — Re-check the baseline
steps.say: Same check as the start. Let's see if that moved.

steps.name: 0:58 — Open Q&A
steps.say: Anonymous question queue is open — ask anything, including things you didn't want to say out loud. I'll keep it open after we leave the room.

steps.name: 0:59 — Guide page: AI Tip of the Day
steps.say: One more small thing before we close — a rotating daily tip lives on the Guide's landing page.

steps.name: 1:00 — Thank you / contact
steps.say: Thanks, everyone. Here's how to find the Guide again and reach me afterward.
